sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: What
Geographical and administrative division of the Republic of India into **28 States** and **8 Union Territories**.
When
Continuous evolution from **1956 (States Reorganisation Act)** to the latest formation of **Telangana in 2014** and **Ladakh/J&K in 2019**.
Where
Entire territory of India spanning **3,287,263 sq km** across various geographical zones.
Who
Governed by **State Governments** (Chief Ministers & Governors) and **Central Government** (President through Lieutenant Governors/Administrators for UTs).
Why Important
Forms the bedrock of Indian federalism, administrative governance, resource allocation, and direct questions in **UPSSSC PET General Awareness**.
Key Features
**Bicameral legislatures** in select states, varying sizes, unique cultural identities, and constitutional status under **Article 1 to 4 (Part I)** and **Part VIII** of the Indian Constitution.
Significance for UPSSSC PET
High-scoring static GK section covering **capitals, founding dates, reorganization commissions, and executive heads**.
Other Essential Facts
**Rajasthan** is the largest state by area, **Goa** is the smallest state, **Uttar Pradesh** has the highest population and legislative seats.

items.title: 1. Constitutional Framework of States & UTs (Articles 1-4)
items.content:
• **Article 1:** Name and territory of the Union, declaring India as a **'Union of States'** rather than a federation of states.
• **Article 2:** Parliament may admit into the Union of India, or establish, new states on such terms and conditions.
• **Article 3:** Formation of new states and alteration of areas, boundaries, or names of existing states by a **Simple Majority**.
• **Article 4:** Laws made under Articles 2 and 3 to amend the **First and Fourth Schedules** are not considered constitutional amendments under **Article 368**.
• **Mnemonic for Parts:** **U**nion **T**akes **C**itizens **F**ast (**U**nion-Part I, **T**erritory-Part II/Citizenship, **C**itizenship, **F**undamental Rights).

items.title: 2. Evolution & Reorganisation Commissions
items.content:
• **Dhar Commission (1948):** Recommended reorganization on **administrative convenience** rather than linguistic basis.
• **JVP Committee (1948-49):** Composed of **Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel, and Pattabhi Sitaramayya**; rejected linguistic basis temporarily.
• **Fazl Ali Commission (1953-1955):** Also known as the **States Reorganisation Commission (SRC)**; accepted language as the basis of reorganisation.
• **States Reorganisation Act, 1956:** Created **14 States and 6 Union Territories** on **November 1, 1956**.
• **Mnemonic for SRC Members:** **F**azl **K**m **P**anikkar (**F**azl Ali, **K**.M. Panikkar, **H**.N. Kunzru).

items.title: 3. Union Territories: Administration & Special Status
items.content:
• Governed under **Part VIII (Articles 239 to 241)** of the Constitution of India.
• Administered by the **President** acting through an administrator appointed by him (designated as **Lieutenant Governor, Chief Commissioner, or Administrator**).
• **Delhi, Puducherry, and Jammu & Kashmir** possess legislative assemblies and elected Chief Ministers.
• **Andaman & Nicobar Islands** fall under the jurisdiction of the **Calcutta High Court**.
• **Lakshadweep** falls under the jurisdiction of the **Kerala High Court**.

items.title: 4. Recent Reorganisations & Statehood Timelines
items.content:
• **Andhra Pradesh (1953):** First linguistic state created on **October 1, 1953**.
• **Gujarat & Maharashtra (1960):** Bifurcated from the bilingual state of Bombay on **May 1, 1960**.
• **Nagaland (1963):** 16th State of the Indian Union.
• **Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand, Jharkhand (2000):** Created in **November 2000** under the Vajpayee government.
• **Telangana (2014):** 29th State created on **June 2, 2014**.
• **Jammu & Kashmir Reorganisation Act (2019):** Bifurcated J&K into two UTs: **Jammu & Kashmir** and **Ladakh** on **October 31, 2019**.

items.title: 5. Special Provisions for States (Article 371 Series)
items.content:
• **Article 371:** Special provisions for **Maharashtra and Gujarat** (establishment of separate development boards).
• **Article 371A:** Special provisions for **Nagaland** (religious/social practices, customary law protection).
• **Article 371B & 371C:** Special provisions for **Assam** and **Manipur** respectively.
• **Article 371F:** Special provisions for **Sikkim** (admitted via **36th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1975**).
• **Article 371J:** Special provisions for the **Hyderabad-Karnataka region** (Karnataka).

Formalized rejection of pure linguistic division at that time.

Fazl Ali, K.M. Panikkar, H.N. Kunzru
Led to the landmark **States Reorganisation Act, 1956**.
36th Amendment Act (1975)

Converted Sikkim from an associate state to the **22nd State**.
69th Amendment Act (1991)
Granted special status to Delhi as **National Capital Territory (NCT)**
Created a 70-member assembly and a council of ministers for Delhi.
J&K Reorganisation Act (2019)
Passed in Parliament, effective from October 31, 2019
Converted J&K state into two separate **Union Territories**.
Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu Act (2019)
Merged two UTs into one single UT
Reduced total number of UTs to **8** effective January 26, 2020.
Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act (2014)
Bifurcated AP to create Telangana
Telangana became the **29th State** on June 2, 2014.

items.definition: Remember the sequence using the order of creation in Nov 2000: **C.U.J.** (Chhattisgarh on 1st Nov, Uttarakhand on 9th Nov, Jharkhand on 15th Nov). Mnemonic: **C**hhattisgarh **U**nder **J**harkhand.

Use the mnemonic sentence: **'CHALO DIL DO APNI LADAKH'** -> **CH**andigarh, **A**ndaman & Nicobar, **L**akshadweep, **O**disha (no, NCT Delhi), **D**aman & Diu & Dadra & Nagar Haveli, **P**uducherry, **J**ammu & Kashmir, **L**adakh.

items.term: Trick 3: Seven Sister States of Northeast India
items.definition: Use the acronym **'ATM Machine'** + 3N: **A**ssam, **T**ripura, **M**eghalaya, **N**agaland, **M**anipur, **M**izoram, and **A**runachal Pradesh (Note: Sikkim is a brother, not a sister state).

items.term: Trick 4: States with Bicameral Legislature ( ವಿಧಾನಮಂಡಲ )
items.definition: Use the mnemonic **'VOTERS K'**: **V**ihar, **O**rissa (No - removed), **T**elangana, **E**l (no), **R**ajasthan (no), **S** - **U**ttar Pradesh, **M**aharashtra, **A**ndhra Pradesh, **K**arnataka, **B**ihar. Active 6 states: **UP, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana**.
Associate **Andhra Pradesh** with **1953** and leader **Potti Sreeramulu** who died after a 56-day hunger strike for a separate Telugu state.

items.term: Trick 6: Largest and Smallest States by Area
items.definition: Area mnemonic: **R M M** (Rajasthan is largest, Madhya Pradesh second, Maharashtra third). Smallest state: **Goa**.
Top 3 most populous states in order: **U.M.B.** (**U**ttar Pradesh, **M**aharashtra, **B**ihar).

items.term: Mistake 1: Confusing Telangana's Formation Date with Division
items.definition: Students often confuse Telangana's formation year (**2014**) with the creation of Chhattisgarh/Uttarakhand/Jharkhand (**2000**).

items.term: Mistake 2: Total Number of States and UTs
items.definition: Remember that India currently has **28 States and 8 UTs** (not 29 states, as J&K was reclassified into UTs, and Dadra & Nagar Haveli + Daman & Diu were merged into 1 UT).
Sikkim was **not** a part of India at Independence; it became a protectorate, then an associate state, and finally the **22nd full State in 1975**.
Only **three** UTs have Legislative Assemblies: **Delhi, Puducherry, and Jammu & Kashmir**. Chandigarh, Ladakh, Lakshadweep, Andaman & Nicobar, and Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu do not.

items.term: Mistake 5: High Court Jurisdiction of UTs
items.definition: Do not assume every UT has its own High Court. For example, **Andaman & Nicobar** comes under Calcutta HC, **Lakshadweep** under Kerala HC, and **Ladakh** under J&K and Ladakh HC.
Students frequently confuse the capitals of **Meghalaya (Shillong)**, **Manipur (Imphal)**, and **Nagaland (Kohima)**. Memorize them distinctly.
Article **2** is for admitting **new foreign territories** into the Union, while Article **3** deals with internal redrawing, renaming, and carving out new states from existing Indian territory.
Part I of the Indian Constitution (**Articles 1 to 4**) deals with the Union and its territory.
India is described as a **'Union of States'** in Article 1, indicating that the federation is not the result of an agreement among states.
Only **Parliament** has the power to admit, establish, alter boundaries, or rename states under Article 3 by a **simple majority**.
The **States Reorganisation Act, 1956**, implemented the recommendations of the **Fazl Ali Commission**, reorganizing India into **14 States and 6 UTs**.
Presently, India comprises **28 States and 8 Union Territories**.
**Rajasthan** covers the largest geographical area among Indian states.
**Goa** is the smallest state by area in India.
**Uttar Pradesh** holds the highest population and sends the maximum number of MPs to Parliament.
**Telangana** is the 29th state formed on **June 2, 2014** (though total states count is 28 due to J&K reorganization).
**Delhi, Puducherry, and Jammu & Kashmir** have elected legislative assemblies and Chief Ministers.
Several states enjoy special provisions under **Articles 371 to 371J** to protect regional and tribal interests.
Only **6 states** currently have a bicameral legislature (Legislative Council + Legislative Assembly).

upscNotes.content: For UPSSSC PET, always memorize the exact dates and years of creation for newly formed states like Chhattisgarh (Nov 1, 2000), Uttarakhand (Nov 9, 2000), Jharkhand (Nov 15, 2000), and Telangana (June 2, 2014).
Revise the High Court jurisdictions for Union Territories (e.g., Lakshadweep under Kerala HC, Andaman & Nicobar under Calcutta HC) as these are favorite tricky questions in UP exams.
Do not get confused by the total number of Union Territories. After the merger of Daman & Diu and Dadra & Nagar Haveli in 2020, the total count of UTs is 8, not 7 or 9.

Questions often test whether a State Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) can be created or abolished by the State Assembly alone. Remember, it requires a resolution passed by the State Assembly by a special majority followed by an Act of Parliament by a simple majority under Article 169.

keyTakeaways: India is a Union of 28 States and 8 Union Territories governed under Part I and Part VIII of the Constitution.
The States Reorganisation Act of 1956 restructured India on a linguistic basis following the Fazl Ali Commission report.
Article 3 empowers the Parliament to alter state boundaries, areas, or names using a simple majority without constitutional amendment under Article 368.
Andhra Pradesh was the first linguistic state created in 1953, and Telangana is the most recent major state formed in 2014.
Only Delhi, Puducherry, and Jammu & Kashmir among the 8 Union Territories possess their own Legislative Assemblies.
Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state, while Rajasthan is the largest by area and Goa is the smallest by area.
